question: Which statement best describes Route groups (group) that don't affect the URL?
options: Wrapping a folder name in parentheses — `(marketing)`, `(shop)` — creates a route group that is purely organizational: it groups routes (and lets them share a layout) WITHOUT adding a segment to the URL. So `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx` still resolves to `/about`. This is how you split a big app into sections without polluting the path.

Each route group can have its own `layout.tsx`, so all routes inside `(marketing)` share a marketing header/footer while `(shop)` shares a store chrome — even though their URLs sit at the same level. This keeps unrelated sections from being forced into one shared layout.

A folder prefixed with `@`, like `@team` or `@analytics`, defines a NAMED SLOT that a parent layout receives as a prop alongside `children`. The layout can render several independent pages — a dashboard plus a side panel plus analytics — simultaneously, each with its own loading/error state and independent navigation.

By giving two route groups their OWN root layout (each with its own `<html>` and `<body>`) and removing the top-level `app/layout.tsx`, you can ship genuinely different shells — e.g. a marketing site and a logged-in app — under one project. Navigating between groups triggers a full page load because the root layout changes.

Intercepting conventions — `(.)` same level, `(..)` one level up, `(...)` from root — let one route render ANOTHER route's content within the current layout.
